title: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Military Invalidity Payments Means Testing) Bill 2024
short_title: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Military Invalidity Payments Means Testing) Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend the Social Security Act 1991 and the Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986 so that certain military invalidity pensions have a clear footing in the income support means test.
It would create a new military invalidity pension income stream category, assessed by subtracting a special reduction amount from the gross annual payment and exempt from the assets test.
The new rules would apply from the day after Royal Assent, whenever the income stream began, and earlier assessments made on the pre-Douglas understanding of the law would be validated.
changes: The new definition would cover invalidity pay under the Defence Force Retirement and Death Benefits Act 1973 and invalidity pensions under the Military Superannuation and Benefits Act 1991.
It would let the Secretary, and the Commission under the Veterans' Entitlements Act, add further income streams to the definition by legislative instrument.
Military invalidity pension income streams would be treated as fully asset-test exempt under both Acts, not as partially asset-test exempt income streams.
Non-military income streams added by instrument would have the special reduction amount capped at 10% of the annual payment under the Social Security Act only.
Past assessments of ordinary income from the affected payments for days before commencement would be taken to have always been valid.
The departmental cost is put at $11.9 million over the forward estimates from 2023-24 to 2027-28.
summary.affected: Veterans and their partners receiving income support alongside invalidity pensions from the Military Superannuation and Benefits Scheme or the Defence Force Retirement and Death Benefits Scheme are affected.
